newsitem.title: USA: U S West files challenge to FCC phone rules.
newsitem.headline: U S West files challenge to FCC phone rules.

text.p: U S West Inc said Thursday it asked the U.S. Court of Appeals here to overturn major parts of the Federal Communications Commission's new rules designed to open the local phone market to competition.
The company also said that on Friday it will ask the FCC to set aside portions of the August 8 order.

"Our main concern is that the FCC has taken a law we support -- the (1996 Telecommunications) Act -- and a concept we strongly support -- full-blown telecommunications competition -- and turned it on its head," U S West Chairman Richard McCormick said in a statement.
The company joins a growing list of other local phone providers and state regulators who are challenging the FCC's "interconnection" rules in court.
But lawyers predict the challenges will fail and that the main portions of the rules will survive in court.

U S West said its appeal contends -- among other things -- that the FCC exceeded its statutory authority in the new telecommunications law by undermining the intercompany negotiations process established by the law.
The company also argues that the FCC violated the Fifth Amendment of the U.S. Constitution by prohibiting companies from recovering the cost of past investments in the local phone network.
Major long-distance companies have not formally challenged the new rules.
